text:
It's not a crime, but your partner has a point for some movies.

You're allowed to watch however you like. People have always skimmed books, skipped scenes, and watched on a laptop with a phone in hand. Nobody is harmed if you watch a mediocre thriller at 1.5x.

Where your partner is right is that pacing is part of what some films are made of. A slow Tarkovsky or Kelly Reichardt film at 1.5x isn't the same film anymore. Comedy also suffers, because timing is most of the joke, and so do music and sound design, which are tuned to a specific tempo. If you're speeding through those, you're mostly getting the plot summary.

If slow pacing makes you restless in almost everything now, that's worth noticing too. Maybe you'd enjoy the movie more at normal speed with your phone out of reach, or maybe you'd enjoy something else more.

A fair compromise: watch at 1x when you're watching together or when your partner picked the film, and use 1.25x to 1.5x on your own for dialogue-heavy or plot-driven stuff you'd otherwise abandon. Speeding up a movie you'd have turned off anyway beats not finishing it.
